lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Thank you for calling Open Gong support, this is Sam speaking. Quick heads-up before we start — this call is recorded for quality and training purposes. What can I help you with today?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Hi Sam. My name is Rachel, I'm the office manager at Hartley & Co. I'm calling because we've been charged twice on our latest invoice.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I'm sorry to hear that, Rachel. Let's get it sorted. Can I start with the email address on the account?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: It's billing@hartleyco.com.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Thanks. And can you confirm the company name on the account, just for verification?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Hartley & Co. We're an accounting firm, if that helps you find us.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Perfect, that matches what I have. Now, tell me about the charges — when did they come through?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Both on Monday the tenth. Two separate charges, four hundred and eighty dollars each, a few minutes apart.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Two charges of four hundred and eighty on the tenth. Let me pull up your billing history — bear with me for a moment.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: No problem. I've got the bank statement open in front of me if you need reference numbers.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: That may come in handy. Okay, I have your account up... and yes, I can see two payments processed on the tenth.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: So it's not just something odd on our statement. Good, I was starting to doubt myself.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: No, you're right — there are definitely two charges on our side as well. Let me dig into what generated the second one.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Please do. And I'll be honest with you, Sam — this is the second billing issue this year. In February an invoice went out with the wrong seat count and it took two weeks to get corrected.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I'm really sorry about that, and I completely understand the frustration of it happening again. My goal is to have this fully resolved before we hang up, not in two weeks.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: That would be a very welcome change.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: While I'm looking — did anyone on your side make changes to the plan recently?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Yes, actually. Our director upgraded us from the Team plan to the Business plan last week, so we could add the new hires.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: That lines up with what I'm seeing. The upgrade went through on the ninth. Give me one more minute here.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Sure, take your time.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Okay, found it. When the upgrade was processed, the system created a brand new subscription for the Business plan but never closed out your old Team subscription. So on the tenth, both subscriptions billed at the same time. That's your double charge.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: So we were being billed for two plans at once?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: For this one cycle, yes. The duplicate was only created on the ninth, so this is the first and only time it billed. It's clearly an error on our side, and it's straightforward to fix.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Okay. So what happens now?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Two things, and I'm doing both right now. First, I'm cancelling the duplicate Team subscription so it can never bill you again. Second, I'm issuing a full refund of four hundred and eighty dollars for the duplicate charge.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: And the Business plan we actually want stays untouched?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Exactly — your Business plan is unaffected. Only the leftover Team subscription is being removed.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Good. How long will the refund take? Our accountant closes the books at the end of the month.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: The refund is submitted on our side today, and it typically lands back on your card within five to seven business days, depending on your bank.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Five to seven business days — that's before month-end, so that works.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: It should be with you well before then. Alright, the duplicate subscription is now cancelled, and the refund has been submitted. It will show up as a credit from Open Gong on the same card that was charged.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Will I get something in writing? My accountant is going to want a paper trail for this.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Absolutely. I'll send a confirmation email to billing@hartleyco.com within the hour, with the refund reference number and the cancellation details for the duplicate subscription.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Perfect. That's exactly what I need.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: One more thing, Rachel. Given this is the second billing problem you've dealt with this year, I'd like to apply a fifty dollar credit to your account for the inconvenience. It will come off your next invoice automatically.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Oh — well, that's appreciated. You didn't have to do that.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: It's the least we can do. I'm also adding a note so our billing team double-checks your next invoice before it goes out.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: That does give me some peace of mind, honestly.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Let me recap so we're on the same page. The duplicate Team subscription is cancelled. A refund of four hundred and eighty dollars is on its way and should arrive within five to seven business days. A fifty dollar credit will appear on your next invoice. And a confirmation email with the refund reference is coming to you within the hour.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: That covers everything. Honestly, this went a lot smoother than the last time.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I'm glad to hear that. Is there anything else I can help you with while I have you?

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: No, that was the only thing. Thank you for sorting it so quickly, Sam.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: You're very welcome. One last thing — if the refund hasn't appeared after seven business days, just reply to the confirmation email and I'll chase it with our payment processor directly.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Will do. Thanks again.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Thank you for calling, Rachel. Have a great day.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: You too. Bye.

follow_up_email.subject: Your refund is on its way — duplicate charge resolved (Hartley & Co)
follow_up_email.body:
Hi Rachel,

Thanks for calling in today, and again, I'm sorry about the duplicate charge.

Here's a written recap for your records:
- Cause: the plan upgrade on the 9th created a second subscription that wasn't closed out, so both billed on the 10th
- Fixed: the duplicate Team subscription is cancelled and can't bill again — your Business plan is unchanged
- Refund: $480.00 submitted today, refund reference OG-RF-58214. It should appear on the same card within 5-7 business days, well before your month-end close
- Credit: a $50 goodwill credit will come off your next invoice automatically
- Extra check: I've flagged your account so our billing team reviews your next invoice before it goes out

If the refund hasn't appeared after 7 business days, just reply to this email and I'll chase it with our payment processor directly.

Best,
Sam
Open Gong Support
